"You are running as a quick-create assistant for a Multica workspace.

A user captured the following input via the quick-create modal. There is NO existing issue. Your job is to create a well-formed issue from this input with a single `multica issue create` command.

User input:
> set remote : [https://github.com/TaQuangKhoi/openfarm.git](https://github.com/TaQuangKhoi/openfarm.git) , read [https://taquangkhoi.com/en/products/open-farm](https://taquangkhoi.com/en/products/open-farm) and [https://devpost.com/software/open-farm-sui](https://devpost.com/software/open-farm-sui) to understand the concept that project want to build. I want to join a hackathon from Sui , read more at [https://overflow.sui.io/](https://overflow.sui.io/) and I want to join this track : [https://mystenlabs.notion.site/defi-payments-problem-statement](https://mystenlabs.notion.site/defi-payments-problem-statement). Can you help me to choose the right track for openfarm? You can help me create AGENT dot md and README dot md too

Field rules:

- **title**: required. A concise but semantically rich summary. If the input references external resources (PRs, issues, URLs), use your judgment on whether fetching the resource would produce a meaningfully better title — e.g. \"review PR #123\" → \"Review PR #123: Refactor auth module to OAuth2\". Strip filler words but preserve key semantic information.

- **description**: The description is the executing agent's primary context. Aim for high fidelity — they should grasp the user's intent as if they had read the raw input themselves. Use a two-section structure:

  1. **User request** — Faithfully restate what the user wants in their own words. Preserve specific names, identifiers, file paths, code snippets, and technical terms verbatim. Strip non-spec material before writing it (this is removal, not paraphrasing): verbal routing wrappers about creating the issue or routing it (e.g. \"create an issue\", \"分配给 X\", \"让 @X 处理\") and pure conversational fillers (e.g. \"对吧？\"). When in doubt, keep it.

     CC exception: `multica issue create` has no `--subscriber` flag, and the platform auto-subscribes members whose `[@Name](mention://member/<uuid>)` link appears in the description. When the user wrote \"cc @Y\", strip the verbal \"cc\" wrapper from the User request body and append a final `CC: <mention link(s)>` line to the description so the cc routing still fires.

  2. **Context** — include ONLY when the input cited external resources AND you successfully fetched them AND they produced verifiable facts worth recording. Summarize facts only (e.g. \"PR #45 changes auth to JWT\"), not interpretation or unsolicited reference implementations. If you have nothing factual to add, omit the section entirely — never use it as an apology log for resources you could not fetch.

  Hard rules: never invent requirements, implementation details, or acceptance criteria the user did not express; never reduce multi-sentence input to a single vague sentence; never echo the title.

- **priority**: one of `urgent`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, or omit. Map P0/P1 → urgent/high; \"asap\" → urgent. If unspecified, omit.

- **assignee**:
    - When the user names someone (\"assign to X\" / \"@X\"), call `multica workspace member list --output json`, `multica agent list --output json`, and `multica squad list --output json` and find the matching entity by display name. Squads are first-class assignees too — a squad name (e.g. \"Super Human\") routes work to the squad leader, who then delegates. On a clean unambiguous match, prefer `--assignee-id <uuid>` using the `user_id` (member) or `id` (agent or squad) from that JSON — UUID matching is exact and robust to name collisions in workspaces with overlapping names. `--assignee <name>` (fuzzy) is acceptable as a fallback when names are unambiguous. On no match or ambiguous match, do NOT pass either flag — instead append a final line to the description: `Unrecognized assignee: X`.
    - Treat bare @-routing as an assignee directive even when the user did not write the English word \"assign\". This includes Chinese imperatives like `让 @独立团 review 这个 PR`, `给 @X 处理`, or `交给 @X`; strip the leading `@`/`＠` before matching display names. Do not keep that routing wrapper or `@Name` in the description unless it is a true CC-style notification rather than ownership. If the matched entity is a squad, pass the squad's `id` as `--assignee-id`, not the leader agent's id.
    - When the user did NOT name an assignee, default to YOURSELF: pass `--assignee-id \"77e3b9a6-ae20-4f72-96f3-69517c9d31d4\"` (your agent UUID). The picker agent is the expected owner because the user opened quick-create with you selected — never leave the issue unassigned. Use the UUID flag, not `--assignee <name>`, so the assignment is unambiguous even when other agents share part of your name.

- **project**: required for this run. Pass `--project \"3e662b8f-d7e1-4817-a725-f47323e31e25\"` so the new issue lands in project \"skills\" (the user picked it in the quick-create modal). Do not infer a different project from the prompt text — the modal selection is authoritative.
- **status**: omit (defaults to `todo`).
- **attachments**: do NOT pass `--attachment`. The flag only accepts LOCAL file paths. Any image URL in the user input is already markdown — keep it inline in `--description` instead.

Output format:
- Run exactly one `multica issue create --output json` invocation. Do not retry for any reason — even on non-zero exit. The issue may already exist; another attempt would create a duplicate.
- Parse the JSON response to read the created issue's `identifier` (preferred) or `id` (fallback). Do not scrape human output and do not assume any workspace issue prefix such as `MUL-`; workspaces can use custom prefixes.
- After success, print exactly one line: `Created <identifier-or-id>: <title>` and exit. No commentary, no follow-up tool calls.
- Do NOT call `multica issue get` or `multica issue comment add` — there is no issue to query or comment on.
- On CLI error or JSON parse error, exit with the error as the only output. The platform writes a failure notification automatically.
"
I'll fetch the referenced resources to build a richer description, then create the issue.

# Open Farm SUI

Open Farm SUI turns liquidity providing into an interactive farming game on the SUI blockchain. Users tend to virtual crops that represent their LP positions in Cetus CLMM pools — each crop is a dynamic NFT whose appearance evolves based on real-time DeFi metrics like fee earnings and price range health. The idea was conceived by Henry Nguyen; built and submitted to the Hack the Farm hackathon.

SuiDeFiMoveNext.jsNFTCetus CLMM

Features

-   ✦Farm Slots & Land System — plant seeds representing LP tokens from Cetus CLMM pools
-   ✦Dynamic NFT Crops — appearance evolves based on fee earnings, price range health, and time in position
-   ✦Social & Competitive Elements — leaderboards, farm sharing, and achievement systems
-   ✦Educational Onboarding — farming metaphors abstract away DeFi complexity for new users
-   ✦Smart Contracts in Move — farm management, crop lifecycle, NFT minting/evolution, and reward distribution
-   ✦What's next: Multi-Protocol Support, DAO Governance, Mobile App, and Cross-Chain expansion

## FAQ

### What is Sui Overflow 2026?

Sui Overflow 2026 is a global online hackathon where developers and builders create projects on Sui across focused tracks.

### Why should I participate in Sui Overflow 2026?

Itʼs an opportunity to build alongside a global community, explore new ideas, and gain recognition through prizes and ecosystem support.

### When can I register for Sui Overflow 2026?

Pre-registration is now open. Sign up to receive updates, early access, and next steps as the hackathon approaches.

### Who can participate in Sui Overflow 2026?

Anyone is welcome to participate in Sui Overflow 2026! Whether you're a seasoned Web3 developer, a designer, or just starting to explore blockchain, youʼre welcome to join. There are no experience requirements - just bring your ideas and motivation.

### Can I submit to more than one track?

You must select the one track that best represents your project.

### Are there track-specific resources or mentors?

Yes. Each track will have dedicated mentors and workshops. Stay tuned for updates.

### How can I learn about Sui and Move to prepare for Sui Overflow?

There are many developer resources available to help you get started with Sui and Move. Access the [Sui developer docs](https://docs.sui.io/), explore developer tools and resources on the [Sui developer portal](https://www.sui.io/developers), or take a self-paced [intro course to Move](https://github.com/sui-foundation/sui-move-intro-course) to get started.

If you have additional questions, please contact [devrel@sui.io](mailto:devrel@sui.io) or [@suidevelopers](https://x.com/suidevelopers)

  --description-stdin <<'EOF'
## User request

Set the git remote for this project to https://github.com/TaQuangKhoi/openfarm.git

Read the following resources to understand the concept the project wants to build:
- https://taquangkhoi.com/en/products/open-farm
- https://devpost.com/software/open-farm-sui

I want to join a hackathon from Sui (read more at https://overflow.sui.io/), and I want to join this track: https://mystenlabs.notion.site/defi-payments-problem-statement

Help me choose the right track for OpenFarm. Also help me create `AGENT.md` and `README.md`.

## Context

**OpenFarm SUI** (taquangkhoi.com): Turns liquidity providing into an interactive farming game on the Sui blockchain. Users tend virtual crops that represent their LP positions in Cetus CLMM pools — each crop is a dynamic NFT whose appearance evolves based on real-time DeFi metrics (fee earnings, price range health, time in position). Stack: Sui, Move, Next.js, NFTs, Cetus CLMM. Features include farm slots/land system, dynamic NFT crops, social/competitive elements (leaderboards, farm sharing, achievements), educational onboarding via farming metaphors, and Move smart contracts for farm management, crop lifecycle, NFT minting/evolution, and reward distribution. Originally conceived by Henry Nguyen; previously submitted to the "Hack the Farm" hackathon. Links: Devpost (devpost.com/software/open-farm-sui), X (@OpenFarmSUI), demo video (youtube.com/watch?v=ROXPz9D5m_4).

**Sui Overflow 2026** (overflow.sui.io): Sui's global online virtual hackathon, May–August 2026, $1M+ in prizes & seed funding. Registration is open. Each project must select exactly ONE track. Relevant tracks for OpenFarm:
- **DeFi & Payments** (Core Track) — the track the user linked (mystenlabs.notion.site/defi-payments-problem-statement). Create financial primitives or payment rails on Sui that are fast, seamless, and usable in real-world scenarios. Core track prizes: $30K / $15K / $10K / $7.5K.
- **DeepBook** (Specialized Track, $70K pool) — trading or liquidity applications powered by DeepBook's on-chain orderbook.
- **Entertainment & Culture / ONE Championship** (consumer-facing apps in gaming, NFTs, sports, media).
The Notion problem-statement page for the DeFi & Payments track is JavaScript-gated and could not be fetched directly.
EOF
